## What to remember {#revision-essentials}

- The output head maps the final state at one position to V logits, where V is the vocabulary size. Each score corresponds to a candidate token.
- A logit is a real-valued score and can be negative. Softmax converts logit differences to normalized probabilities.
- Output logits are indexed by vocabulary entries. Attention scores for a query are indexed by the positions it can access.
- Softmax preserves the ranking of logits while producing a distribution. Knowing the ranking alone does not give the gap between the probabilities.

## Recall from memory {#revision-check}

With a vocabulary of 50,000 tokens and a hidden dimension of 768, how many logits are emitted per position?

<details>
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

50,000. The head projects the 768 components to one score for each vocabulary token.

</details>
